Open a dataset as a lazy query

Source: R/query.R
store_open.Rd

The usual way to work with a dataset: open it, describe the rows you want with dplyr verbs, and read them into R with collect(). Opening reads no data; the query is built from the files the dataset's catalog names (the folder is never listed). The query is transformed with the dplyr verbs filter(), select(), mutate(), rename(), arrange(), distinct(), head(), and run with collect() (an R data frame), compute() (rows kept in memory as Arrow data), pull() or glimpse(). Arrow pushes filters and column selection into the scan, so only the needed files, row groups and columns are read. store_read() is the shortcut for store_open(), filter(), select() and collect() in one call.

Usage

store_open(
  st,
  dataset,
  version = NULL,
  engine = c("arrow", "duckdb"),
  con = NULL,
  mode = "native",
  spatial = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_query'
print(x, ..., n = NULL)

Arguments

st

A store connection made by store_connect().

dataset

Name of the dataset: the full name, or its last part when that is unique in the store.

version

NULL for the current version, or the 16 hex characters of an earlier version kept in the history (see store_history()). Only NULL with engine = "duckdb".

engine

"arrow" (the default) for a lazy Arrow query of class rcs_query; "duckdb" for a dbplyr table on the dataset's DuckDB view (see store_duckdb() and vignette("duckdb")), of class rcs_duckdb_tbl. Every dbplyr verb works on it; its collect() restores the R types (factor levels, difftime units, bit64::integer64, rcs_h3 cells) and the geometry as for the Arrow engine, and drops .rcs_id. It needs the packages duckdb, DBI and dbplyr.

con

With engine = "duckdb": NULL for an in-memory connection that the package keeps, one per store, until the end of the session; or a DuckDB connection made with bigint = "integer64", on which the view is created (or refreshed) as by store_duckdb(st, con = con).

mode, spatial

With engine = "duckdb": as in store_duckdb().

x

A query made by store_open() with engine = "arrow".

...

Passed to the tibble print method (for example width).

n

Number of rows to print; NULL uses the option rcs.print_rows (10).

Value

store_open(): a lazy query of class rcs_query, or with engine = "duckdb" a lazy dbplyr table of class rcs_duckdb_tbl. print(): x, invisibly.

Details

  • A filter whose columns are all partition columns is first evaluated on the partition values recorded in the catalog: only the files of the matching partitions are opened.

  • store_intersects() adds a spatial filter.

  • collect() returns a tibble, or an sf object for a geospatial dataset whose geometry is read, with the catalog's coordinate reference system. It restores the R types Arrow does not restore by itself (difftime units, bit64::integer64, factor levels, plain list columns) and drops the row identifier .rcs_id that the package adds to geospatial data; the columns h3, bbox and h3_p<r> are returned, the cells as rcs_h3 vectors.

The query reads from the location chosen as for store_read(), with the catalogs held by the connection. Unlike store_read(), it never copies the dataset to a secondary location.

Printing

Printing a query reads its first rows, and only those: head(n + 1) of the query, the exact test of a spatial filter included, so that it can tell whether more rows exist without counting them. It opens the data files it needs. The first n rows are shown as a tibble under a header:

  • Dataset: the full name, the number of rows and columns, and the kind. The number of rows comes from the catalog when the query is the dataset itself, with columns selected, renamed or computed; after a filter, a spatial filter or any other verb it is shown as ??. The number of columns is that of the data frame collect() returns.

  • Location: the location read (primary or secondary <n>, local or GCS).

  • Version: the first 8 characters of the version, current or earlier.

  • Files: the files kept of the dataset's files, (pruned) when a filter on partition columns or a spatial filter dropped some.

  • Spatial: the spatial filter, when set.

  • Filter: the row filter, or (with spatial predicate) when a spatial filter is set.

The footer says how many rows are not shown (more rows when the total is not known, more rows may exist while an exact spatial test is pending) and reminds that collect() reads the rows into R. A table opened with engine = "duckdb" prints as any dbplyr table.

See also

store_read(), store_intersects(), rcs_query-dplyr, store_duckdb().

Examples

location <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-open")
st <- store_connect(location, create = TRUE)
store_write(st, rcs_sim_table(500), "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales", description = "Simulated daily sales.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"), partition = "year"
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 500 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-open  2/2
#>   files sent  38.3 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
q <- store_open(st, "daily")
q
#> # Dataset:  sales/daily [500 x 15] (table)
#> # Location: primary (local)
#> # Version:  a6caa62a (current)
#> # Files:    2 of 2
#>    shop_id date        year product   qty price promo grade delivered      big
#>      <int> <date>     <int> <fct>   <int> <dbl> <lgl> <ord> <date>     <int64>

#>  2       1 2023-01-24  2023 p19        42 182.  FALSE low   2023-01-28   3 e 2
#>  3       1 2023-01-28  2023 p17        12  83.4 TRUE  mid   2023-01-29   2 e 2
#>  4       1 2023-03-12  2023 p07        21 129.  FALSE low   NA           6 e 2
#>  5       1 2023-03-15  2023 p18        29 157.  FALSE mid   2023-03-25   9 e15
#>  6       1 2023-03-27  2023 p08        NA  81.9 FALSE high  2023-04-03   9 e15
#>  7       1 2023-04-14  2023 p06        10 152.  TRUE  high  2023-04-16   3.e 2
#>  8       1 2023-05-11  2023 p04        39 180.  TRUE  mid   2023-05-18   9 e15
#>  9       1 2023-05-30  2023 p18        43 193.  FALSE high  2023-06-09   9 e15
#> 10       1 2023-06-04  2023 p08        28 153.  FALSE low   2023-06-13   8 e 2
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: wait <drtn>, note <chr>, tags <list>, ts <dttm>,
#> #   ts_local <dttm>
#> # ℹ 490 more rows
#> # ℹ Use `collect()` to read the rows into R.
print(q, n = 3)
#> # Dataset:  sales/daily [500 x 15] (table)
#> # Location: primary (local)
#> # Version:  a6caa62a (current)
#> # Files:    2 of 2
#>   shop_id date        year product   qty price promo grade delivered      big
#>     <int> <date>     <int> <fct>   <int> <dbl> <lgl> <ord> <date>     <int64>

#> 3       1 2023-01-28  2023 p17        12  83.4 TRUE  mid   2023-01-29    2e 2
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: wait <drtn>, note <chr>, tags <list>, ts <dttm>,
#> #   ts_local <dttm>

q |>
  dplyr::filter(year == 2024, qty > 40) |>
  dplyr::select(shop_id, date, qty) |>
  dplyr::collect()
